pages.name: World Generation Procedure
pages.html:
World Generation Procedure

If a world is present, use the following procedures to generate the main world of a system.

  • Hexadecimal Planetary Code: Each planet will have a hexadecimal code referred to as the Universal World Code (UWC) to indicate the primary details of a planet, including additional information such as its name, hex location on a map, bases (if any), trade codes, and its Travel Zone code.
  • Example: Chadwick-3: BA6A743-9 N RI WA A
    • Name (Chadwick-3), Hex Location (0205), Starport (B), Size (A), Atmosphere (6), Water Amount (A), Population (7), Government type (4), Law Level (3), Tech Level (9), Naval Base (N), Trade Codes (RI and WA), and Travel Zone (A for Amber Zone)

Starports, bases, trade codes, and travel zones are generated at the end of planet creation.

The following is a breakdown on generating a planet with a Universal World Code.

Work through each step in order. Each step has its own table with explanations and examples.

  • Step 1: Planet Size; Roll 2D-2.
  • Step 2: Atmosphere; Roll 2D-7.
  • Step 3: Hydrographics; Roll 2D -7. Note: Atmosphere 0, 1, A-F has DM -4. Atmosphere 0-1 is Hydro 0.
  • Step 4: Population; Roll 2D-2.
  • Step 5: Government; Roll 2D-7.
  • Step 6: Law Level; Roll 2D-7 + Government Code result from Step 5.

The following steps modify the UWC to include starports, bases, Tech Level, and Trade Codes.

  • Step 7: Starport; Roll 2D. Consult the Starport Table to determine repairs, docking fees, other bases, and more.
  • Step 8: Tech Level; Roll 1D and use the Tech Level table to determine additional DMs based on steps 1-7.
  • Step 9: Trade Codes: Use the Trade Code Table to determine the planet’s tradable commodities.

Results of 1 or less are typically manufactured locations such as orbital space colonies, mining asteroids, or other orbital modules like bases, starports made of manufactured materials, hollowed asteroids, or a combination of both. These locations require a full artificial environment for habitation.

  • Optional: Increase chances of Earth-sized planets. If the referee wants to increase the frequency of Earth-sized planets, they can instead choose to roll 2D+1.

Planets Larger than 16,000km: If desired, a larger planet can be generated by rolling 2D+3.

pages.name: Step 5: Government
pages.html:
Step 5: Government

Step 5: Government; Roll 2D-7 and add the population code to determine the average governing system found on the world.

GovTypeDescription
0NoneNo formal governing structure except for family and interpersonal relationships.
1Company/CorporationFor-profit organizations run by managerial elites who govern the citizenry with corporate organizational structures. Corpo-feudal, private-sponsored colonies, etc.
2Participating DemocracyThe citizens have a direct voice in the ruling functions of government via direct democratic methods and assemblies.
3Self-Perpetuating OligarchyThe government is led by an elite class who maintains power with minimal to no input from the general population.
4Representative DemocracyLaws and government are dictated by elected individuals from the general population.
5Feudal TechnocracyGovernment functions within a caste-based structure driven by technological implementation.
6Captive GovernmentImposed leader or puppet government controlled by an outside government, to govern the local population.
7BalkanisationNo central government. Decentralized, small political governments in perpetual conflict and rivalries driven by philosophical, ecological, economical, and social factors. Laws are determined by the local government.
8Civil Service BureaucracyThe governing duties are driven by government agencies led by groups and individuals with specific expertise from the general population to maintain civil function and services for everyone.
9Impersonal BureaucracyGoverning responsibilities are driven by agencies without input or from the population. Leaders are insulated from the effects of government stagnation.
10 (A)Charismatic DictatorA single leader determines the rule of law and the direction of society, functioning as a representation of the people they govern, prioritising their culture and influence over others.
11 (B)Non-Charismatic LeaderAn impersonal leader who determines the government without popular enthusiasm.
12 (C)Charismatic OligarchyThe population elevates an elite few to drive society in an ideal direction. The chosen few have the full confidence of the many.
13 (D)Religious SovereigntyA religious organisation determines the roles of government, driven by spiritual determinants in law and society.
14 (E)Religious AutocracyA single individual or small group has absolute power over the many via “divine right” and religious authority.
15 (F)Totalitarian OligarchyGovernment is used to force the will of the few onto the many, often with oppressive and coercive methods to maintain and exercise power, to limit the rights of most of the population.

Book p.92

pages.name: Step 6: Law Level
pages.html:
Step 6: Law Level

Step 6: Law Level; Roll 2D-7 and add the government code. Anything banned is also applied to everything listed above it. For example, Law Level 7 bans everything described in Law Level 7 and less. These laws are applied to both citizens and spacers. However, they might not apply to high SOC members of the local society, such as oligarchs, nobles, or other members of high-status minorities on less-equitable planets.

pages.html:
Step 7: Starport and Bases

Step 7: Starport; Roll 2D and use the following dice modifier to determine the main starport on the world, based on the world’s population.

  • Population 8-9: DM +1
  • Population 10+: DM +2
  • Population 3-4: DM -1
  • Population 2 or less: DM -2

Highport is an orbital spaceport that is geo-positioned over the main planetary starport for higher traffic and service.

pages.name: Step 10: Amber and Red Zones
pages.html:
Step 10: Amber and Red Zones

Step 10: Zone Types: Determine if the main world has a Amber or Red Zone.

  • Amber Zone: Amber Zones are places where travelling to is discouraged due to environmental, political, or social reasons that could be dangerous.
  • Amber Zones are designated for the following worlds: Atmosphere 10+ and Government Codes 0, 7, or 10 with Law Level 0 or 9+.
  • Red Zone: Red Zones are banned areas that are either overtly dangerous locations or are sanctuary planets intending to preserve the local ecology, culture, or environment from outside interference. Travelling into Red Zone planets is considered extremely risky, either for personal safety or legally.
  • Red Zones are designated for any planet with an ongoing war, which has a prominent criminal faction that is in control, or is a Low Tech world (5 or less) without a starport.

Book p.95
